question: Insufficiently strong protections and rights are afforded to persons with disabilities under EU law, such as there being no right to travel end-to-end with their mobility equipment. This can mean being denied boarding or mobility equipment being put in the hold, where it can be damaged. To make matters worse, damage to this equipment is then also insufficiently compensated.

All of this can lead to degrading treatment with reports of pilots announcing delays being caused by persons with disabilities who have been forced to wait until all other passengers have boarded first. In light of the above: 1.
Would the Commission support enshrining the right to end-to-end air travel with the use of wheelchairs or other mobility equipment in EU law so that no more people are denied boarding?

Would the Commission support mandating a minimum number of seats and a corresponding percentage of space on each commercial passenger aircraft that would be dedicated for persons with disabilities and their mobility equipment in order to facilitate the aforementioned right to endto-end travel?
Would the Commission be prepared to raise the maximum threshold for compensation in cases where wheelchairs or other mobility equipment are damaged by introducing full liability for such damages?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (29.5.

2024) Persons with disabilities travelling on flights departing from the EU territory or arriving in the EU from a third country on a flight operated by an EU carrier, have the right to travel with their mobility equipment, including electric wheelchairs (subject to advance warning of 48 hours and to possible limitations of space on board the aircraft, and subject to the application of relevant legislation concerning dangerous goods)1.

In 2023, the Commission adopted a legislative proposal2 to improve the enforcement of passenger rights within the EU, which includes provisions intended to ensure, among others, that persons with disabilities are not denied boarding for reasons not related to applicable safety requirements3 or to the size of the aircraft or its doors which makes their embarkation or carriage physically impossible.
In particular, the proposed amendments would oblige carriers to regularly publish statistics about the number of denied boarding situations and related complaints.

National authorities would be obliged to base their monitoring and enforcement activities on a risk assessment, and if they considered that air carriers were unjustly denying transport to persons with disabilities, would be required to take appropriate action.

The Commission would also note that in 2013, it adopted an amending legislative proposal4 which included provisions intended to ensure the full compensation of lost or damaged mobility equipment. Such compensation would be based on a special declaration before the flight of the real value of the mobility equipment that persons with disabilities could make free of charge.
This legislative proposal is still a priority pending Commission proposal.
1 See Article 10 and Annex II of Regulation (EC) No 1107/2006 of the European Parliament and of the Council

of 5 July 2006 concerning the rights of disabled persons and persons with reduced mobility when travelling by air OJ L 204, 26.7.2006, p. 1. 2 COM(2023) 753 final. 3 See Annex IV, Subpart B, CAT.OP.MPA.155 of Commission Regulation (EU) No 965/2012 of 5 October 2012 laying down technical requirements and administrative procedures related to air operations pursuant to Regulation (EC) No 216/2008 of the European Parliament and of the Council, OJ L 296, 25.10.2012, p. 1-148. 4 COM(2013) 130 final.
